challenge.better_approach: Serialise crossings per box (the orchestrator does this today): no code, but every peer waits on every other peer's commit cadence, which is the wait that cost 3195 two refusals.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That artifact.locate can name the ticket a record belongs to (a tickets/<id>-*.log.jsonl path carries it; .artifact-journal.jsonl is shared by all and belongs to no single ticket). The build measures which records locate claims and how.
challenge.prior_art: c1cca2e3dc23 widened the sieve to the whole of both trees (8w/F11/8x); 316bdd5b5e62 refuses another ticket's uncommitted BUILD and already treats records (artifact.locate) as never code dirt; 8u says unclaimed dirt refuses. This narrows only records claimed by another ticket, which is why it goes to Akien as Q#94.
challenge.real_collision: Real, with c1cca2e3dc23/8w, which is why the cast carries Q#94 instead of choosing.

answers.falsifier: RED if another ticket's log/state record still refuses the crossing, if an unclaimed dirty path stops refusing, or if dirty code stops refusing.
answers.from_idea: none, because the orchestrator relayed two measured refusals of 3195b3b834bc's PROVEME on akiendelllinux, raised by WorkingTreeDirtyRed in cairn/tools/base/transitions.py over working_tree_clean in cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py
answers.how: working_tree_clean keeps reading every dirty path in both trees, then drops a path when artifact.locate claims it as a record of a ticket other than the crossing one. What remains still reds. The crossing ticket reaches the sieve through inspect_clean_tree's caller. The design waits on outline Q#94.
answers.traces_to: Law 6 (another ticket's records are that ticket's owner's to commit; my crossing does not judge them) and Law 8 (a crossing is still refused over any code no commit holds, so no green leans on loose code).
answers.what: One peer's ticket records on a box stop refusing another ticket's PROVEME crossing, while unclaimed dirt and code dirt still refuse.

bullets.text: On one box, a peer's ticket records block every other peer's PROVEME (3195 was refused twice on the Dell over d692's and the orchestrator's records). Q#94 asks Akien whether another ticket's claimed records should stop blocking.
